Lines 296-304 fire only when nothing exists at the store path. The branch prints NOT MEASURED YET and states that this is not a build failure, then returns 0. That is exactly the R16.d assertion (store absent means not measured yet, never a build failure), so it is an asserted observation rather than an op category.

Lines 305-311 run when the path exists but readFileSync throws, for example because the path is a directory. The check never gets any text to parse, so it measures nothing, and the exit 1 is a failure to run rather than a verdict on store content. R16.b does not fit: its exit 1 covers malformed lines that leave no usable record, which requires text that was read and parsed. The op:could-not-run definition explicitly includes unreadable input.

Lines 387-393 are the positive outcome of the arming verdict: the floor of usable readings from distinct sessions is met. That is the R16.a observation, and its not-yet branch belongs to the same row. Neither outcome fails the build; both exit 0, as R16.a declares.
